- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+15% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 5–15% based on sentiment shift.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting downward; apply early correction to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% for next 3–7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 3–8% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model may overfit recent momentum; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high unless event-driven.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overreact to short-term noise; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
